details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:682-766 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: "Resolve AI engine", "Stage trusted Claude engine actions", "Install Claude Code CLI" and "Resolve Claude credential" are not gated by VALIDATE_SCHEDULED_MODE, so scheduled runs install the Claude CLI and probe the Claude pool accounts.
  WHY: This contradicts the documented "calls no model" contract and adds cost, latency and credential exposure on every opted-in consumer; the reviewers rated it MAJOR, and the reviewers differ on confidence (3 to 5), not on severity.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:1606 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The sink step runs under always(), and collect_status (lines 1335-1387) fabricates status=error when validation_status.json is missing, so a cancelled scheduled run is treated as red.
  WHY: A cancelled run opens or updates the ai:scheduled-validation-failed issue and sends a Telegram WARNING although the default branch was not shown to be failing; reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:207-211 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A truthy non-list "failures" value makes the [:20] slice raise TypeError, which the except tuple (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError) does not catch.
  WHY: The body generator exits non-zero, the sink takes the body_failed path and files no issue for that red run; reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:107-125,283-287 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The sink does a non-atomic check-then-create of the marker issue, with no lock or idempotency guard.
  WHY: Overlapping scheduled runs or reruns can each create a duplicate issue and send duplicate Telegram WARNINGs; severity is unstated by gemini, NIT per openai and qwen, and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 explicitly dropped this finding as unrealistic.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:~1606 (also 1335-1387, 1346-1358) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A cancelled scheduled run falls back to status=error/raw_status=codex_failure and the sink treats it as red.
  WHY: It opens or updates the "Scheduled validation failing" issue and sends a Telegram WARNING; gating on (success() || failure()) instead of always() fixes it.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:body-generator (`for failure in (data.get("failures") or [])[:20]`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A non-empty dict for failures makes the slice raise an uncaught TypeError.
  WHY: The sink logs body_failed and the red run goes unreported; validate_process.sh always writes a list, so this needs a corrupted result file.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:682-719, 721, 752, 759 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: With tracking_issue=0, "Resolve AI engine" still resolves claude, so the Claude actions are staged, the CLI is installed and claude-pool-token runs.
  WHY: The issue asked that scheduled runs spend no model resources, and the changelog and README say "calls no model"; probes and the CLI install add cost and expose pool credentials.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:Claude pool steps plus workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml `schedule:` trigger | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The schedule trigger is properly scoped, but "no model phases" does not cover the credential-bearing Claude pool steps.
  WHY: Declared-versus-effective gap, the same as the performance finding.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:209 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The loop iterates over data.get("failures") without verifying it is a list.
  WHY: A dict or other truthy non-list value makes the script exit non-zero and leaves no issue opened or updated for a potentially failing run.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:1597-1634 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sink step runs under always() even when the workflow was cancelled.
  WHY: SINK_STATUS is empty and defaults to unknown (red), so a cancellation opens an ai:scheduled-validation-failed issue and sends a Telegram WARNING.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:184-292 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: There is no idempotency guard or lock between finding an existing issue and creating or updating it.
  WHY: Concurrent or overlapping scheduled runs could each create a duplicate issue and send multiple Telegram alerts.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:682-719, 752-765 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The Claude Code install and credential resolution steps are not gated by VALIDATE_SCHEDULED_MODE.
  WHY: Scheduled runs install the Claude CLI and probe every pool account despite the "call no model" requirement, adding cost and latency.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:682-766 (contrast 1281-1288) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: "Resolve AI engine" has no VALIDATE_SCHEDULED_MODE guard, so it can select claude and trigger the stage-actions, install-CLI and resolve-credential steps, which run a Haiku probe per pool account.
  WHY: This contradicts the documented "no model" contract and costs a CLI install and probes every Monday for each opted-in consumer; the fix is `if: env.VALIDATE_SCHEDULED_MODE != 'true'` on the engine step.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:1606 with scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:82-89 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sink runs under always(), so a cancelled run with empty SINK_STATUS is mapped to unknown/red.
  WHY: A cancelled scheduled run opens or updates the issue and sends a Telegram WARNING without evidence that the branch is red.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:207-211 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A truthy non-iterable failures value (e.g. an integer) makes the slice raise TypeError, which is not in the except tuple.
  WHY: The body generator exits non-zero, the sink takes the body_failed path (lines 260-262) and files nothing for that red run.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:1606-1630 and scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:75-80, 99-105, 282-290 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sink step runs with continue-on-error and `|| true`; the review found the trust boundary correct and no declared-vs-effective capability gap.
  WHY: Reported as a NIT with no defect found.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- validate.yml:1335-1357,1604-1610; validate_scheduled_sink.sh:82-89 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A cancelled scheduled run can be reported as a validation failure.
  WHY: Both steps use always(); collect_status creates an error result and the sink treats every status except pass as red, opening or updating the issue and sending a WARNING.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:107-116, 283-287 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Issue deduplication is not atomic.
  WHY: Two scheduled runs can both list issues before either creates one, so both create an issue and send a WARNING; the wrapper has no concurrency group.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:200-210 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A truthy non-list failures value raises an uncaught TypeError.
  WHY: For example "failures": 1 fails the slice at line 207, the script takes the body_failed path, and no issue is filed for that red run.
- validate.yml:682-719,752-765; claude_pool_token.sh:210-225 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Scheduled mode still makes Claude model calls during engine setup.
  WHY: The scheduled-mode flag is not checked by engine resolution or the Claude credential steps, and the default probe setting invokes a Haiku completion once per account despite the documented "calls no model" behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:207-210 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The except clause omits TypeError, so a truthy non-list failures value makes the [:20] slice raise.
  WHY: The body generator exits non-zero, the sink takes the body_failed branch, and no issue is filed for that red run.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:682-719 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: "Resolve AI engine" has no VALIDATE_SCHEDULED_MODE condition, so it can select Claude, and the later steps (lines 752-765) install the Claude CLI and probe pool accounts.
  WHY: This contradicts the "no model" contract and multiplies cost across opted-in consumers.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:107-114, 283-287 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sink checks for an existing issue and later creates one without serialization or an idempotency guard.
  WHY: Concurrent scheduled runs or manual re-runs could create duplicate issues and duplicate Telegram WARNINGs.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:1606 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The sink step runs under always(), so a cancelled run can leave SINK_STATUS empty, which the sink classifies as unknown (red) at sink lines 87-89.
  WHY: A cancelled run opens or updates the failing issue and sends a Telegram WARNING without evidence that the branch is failing.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:107-125, 283-287 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The sink does a check-then-create sequence with no idempotency guard.
  WHY: Overlapping executions can both see an empty list and each open an issue and send a WARNING; the duplicate stays open with no closer.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:1606, 1346-1357; scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:92-97 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sink runs under always(), and collect_status fabricates status=error/raw_status=codex_failure for a cancelled run, which the sink treats as red.
  WHY: A cancelled run opens or updates the issue and sends a Telegram WARNING with a misleading raw status, and the issue only self-corrects on the next passing weekly run.
- scripts/validate_scheduled_sink.sh:207-210 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A truthy non-subscriptable failures value (dict, int, bool) makes the slice raise TypeError, which the except tuple does not catch.
  WHY: The sink takes the body_failed branch and files no issue and sends no WARNING for that red run; the trigger is narrow because validation_result.json is pipeline-written.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:682-719, 752-765 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Job-level engine resolution is not gated, so scheduled runs stage the Claude actions, install the CLI and run claude-pool-token, which probes every pool account.
  WHY: This contradicts the documented zero-model-cost contract and multiplies pool probing across consumers, with unused results.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
